### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. complement component 3 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.435)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-198933, Reactome:R-HSA-9938027)

**Proposed mechanism:** CD40LG (HGNC:2150) —DISRUPTS→ B cell activation and antibody class switching; C3 (HGNC:2540) —DISRUPTS→ Complement system activation; B cell activation and antibody class switching —LEADS_TO→ Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections (HP:0002717); Complement system activation —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002717); B cell activation and antibody class switching —BINDS→ Complement system activation. Mutations in CD40LG disrupt B cell activation and antibody class switching, leading to increased susceptibility to bacterial infections. Mutations in C3 disrupt complement system activation, which also contributes to recurrent bacterial infections. Both pathways are interconnected, as complement activation is crucial for effective B cell responses and clearance of bacterial pathogens.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of increased susceptibility to bacterial infections in patients with homozygous loss-of-function mutations in either CD40LG or C3. _(variant: A common (AF > 0.01) loss-of-function variant in either CD40LG or C3 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream consequences of defects in CD40LG and C3 on immune function can inform therapeutic strategies aimed at bolstering the host's defense against bacterial pathogens, potentially through complementary approaches targeting different aspects of the immune response.

#### 2. obsolete blood group system, landsteiner-wiener  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.361)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-198933)

**Proposed mechanism:** CD40LG (HGNC:2075) —DISRUPTS→ T cell activation (GO:0042110); T cell activation (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Immune cell signaling (GO:0007265); Immune cell signaling (GO:0007265) —LEADS_TO→ Hyper-IgM syndrome type 1 (MONDO:0010626); ICAM4 (HGNC:4760) —DISRUPTS→ B cell activation (GO:0007179); B cell activation (GO:0007179) —LEADS_TO→ Immune cell signaling (GO:0007265); Immune cell signaling (GO:0007265) —LEADS_TO→ Obsolete blood group system, Landsteiner-Wiener (MONDO:0020615). Loss-of-function mutations in CD40LG disrupt T cell activation, leading to Hyper-IgM syndrome type 1. Concurrently, mutations in ICAM4, associated with the Landsteiner-Wiener blood group, may disrupt B cell activation. Both disrupted T cell and B cell activation converge on impaired immune cell signaling, ultimately manifesting as distinct disease phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that CD40LG and ICAM4 function in entirely independent cellular pathways with no convergence at the level of immune cell signaling or downstream cellular processes. _(variant: A common variant (AF > 0.01) in either CD40LG or ICAM4 that demonstrably does not impact protein function or cellular signaling.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the potential overlap in immune cell signaling pathways mediated by CD40LG and ICAM4 could reveal novel therapeutic targets for immune dysregulation, potentially impacting both primary immunodeficiencies and conditions with aberrant immune cell interactions.
